metadata.title: Linear relations of zeroes of the zeta-function

extraction_notes.note: Equations (2.3) and (2.8) are named as results (Ingham's Thm 1, 'the classical result'), but their hypotheses lie in the surrounding sentence ('for any T>0', 'follows if either RH is false ...'). Kept them as equation nodes nested in prose external theorem nodes carrying the hypotheses, rather than retyping the bare equations.

The proofs of Lemmas 1-2 and Theorem 3 sit inside the lemma/theorem environments, so the result nodes' fact spans contain their proofs; proves edges were added by hand since syntax did not state them.

Theorem 1 has no written proof; it follows from Theorem 4 inserted into (2.9)-(2.10) with the kernel f_0, a numerical evaluation not shown. Recorded as uses edges from TP12, ClP1 and DP14 instead of a proof node.

Appendix A's results are two numerical tables (smallest +-1 sums; m-independence bounds); each is represented by the sentence that introduces it as a numerical claim. The binary encoding paragraph for Table 1 is not extracted.
Grosswald's Theorems 1 and 2 are stated in a single sentence; whole-sentence rule kept them as one external theorem node.
The improvement discussion relies on Figures 1-2, whose content is only in images.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{main-algo}
\textbf{Input:} $(k,n,T) \in \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}$.\\
\textbf{Output:} $N_\gamma$.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item Define $K := 10^k$ and $m := \left|\Gamma \cap [0,T]\right|$.
 \item Compute all zeroes, $\gamma$, such that $0 <\gamma \leq T$ to at least $k$ decimal digits of precision.
 \item Sort the elements of $\Gamma \cap [0,T]$ using $\prec$ in (\ref{heavy-order}). Label the {\it heaviest} element $\gamma_1$, the next {\it heaviest} element $\gamma_2$, $\ldots$ , and the least {\it heavy} element $\gamma_m$.
 \item Define $\Gamma' := \left\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2, \cdots , \gamma_n\right\}$.
 \item Let $L_0$ be the reduced lattice basis obtained by running $L(K;\Gamma')$ through LLL-reduction.
 \item Apply Lemma \ref{gram} along with the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1} to $L_0$ to get a candidate for $N_\gamma$.
 \item For all $n < t \leq m$, let $L_t$ be the reduced lattice basis obtained from running $L\left(K;\Gamma' \cup \left\{\gamma_t\right\}\right)$ through LLL-reduction.
 \item Apply Lemma \ref{gram} with the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond2} to every $L_t$ to get $m-n$ additional candidates for $N_\gamma$.
 \item Set $N_\gamma$ to be the minimum of all of the candidates for $N_\gamma$ that were computed in steps 6 and 8.
\end{enumerate}
\caption{Returns an appropriate value for $N_\gamma$ that satisfies the conditions laid out in (\ref{ind1}) and (\ref{ind2}).}

Label the heaviest element gamma_1, the next heaviest element gamma_2, ldots , and the least heavy element gamma_m. item Define Gamma' := left\gamma_1,gamma_2, cdots , gamma_nright\. item Let L_0 be the reduced lattice basis obtained by running L(K;Gamma') through LLL-reduction. item Apply Lemma along with the contrapositive of Lemma to L_0 to get a candidate for N_gamma. item For all n < t leq m, let L_t be the reduced lattice basis obtained from running Lleft(K;Gamma' cup left\gamma_tright\right) through LLL-reduction. item Apply Lemma with the contrapositive of Lemma to every L_t to get m-n additional candidates for N_gamma. item Set N_gamma to be the minimum of all of the candidates for N_gamma that were computed in steps 6 and 8. captionReturns an appropriate value for N_gamma that satisfies the conditions laid out in () and ().

\label{LKGamma}

\cite[Proposition 3.14]{small-vecs}\label{gram}
 Let $L \subset \mathbb{Z}^n$ be a lattice of dimension $m$. Let $\{b_i^*\}$ be the Gram--Schmidt orthogonalization of the basis of $L$. Then $|x|^2 \geq \min\left(|b_i^*|^2\right)$ for any nonzero $x \in L$.

nodes.statement: It is clear that the improved kernel approaches the maximal value quicker than the F\'ejer kernel. To obtain values within 0.01 of the optimal value, the F\'ejer kernel needs to check a total of 30398 zeroes, while the improved kernel only needs to check 6224 zeroes. When a higher precision is needed, the gap widens immensely: to obtain values within 0.001 of the optimal value, the F\'ejer kernel and the improved kernel need to check 399444 and 24043 zeroes, respectively.
